text:
maya (support): FYI, customer AcmeAI opened an urgent ticket — some users can't finish GitHub SSO. They hit a 400 from our callback endpoint with body 'invalid_state_format'. Happens only on their Android WebView builds. Customer provided the callback URL they received:

https://app.acmeai.com/oauth/callback?code=gho_ABC123&state=Q2xpZW50PUFj

They say same flow works on desktop and iOS. Pushing to thread, can someone look? :eyes:

jeff (eng-identity): Thanks — examples are helpful. Can you paste the exact state value? Are there plus signs or padding?

maya (support): Pasting one full example from their logs: 
`state=Q2xpZW50PUFj+MTIzPQ==`
They also sent this note: "only happens when user opens login from our in-app browser (WebView); regular Chrome works."

nina (devex): hmm that state looks like standard base64 with padding (==) and a plus (+). We intentionally validate state to be base64url (no + or /, no padding) — I wonder if our validation is too strict. Which code path rejects it?

jeff (eng-identity): I pulled the identity-service callback logs for that request id. Snippet: 
```
time=2026-02-22T14:12:03Z level=warn svc=identity handler=oauth_callback msg="state validation failed" error=invalid_state_format state="Q2xpZW50PUFj+MTIzPQ=="
http_status=400
```
Looks like our regex in oauth_parser.go only allows [A-Za-z0-9_-] (base64url w/o padding). That explains the reject. I guess mobile WebView is sending regular base64 instead of base64url — maybe their client lib is older.

luke (eng-sre): I reproduced on an Android WebView emulator by forcing state with + and ==. Identity-service returns 400 with the same log. Desktop Chrome (and our tests) use base64url so we missed this.

maya (support): Customer asks for workaround — they can't release an app patch fast. Any temporary fixes?

jeff (eng-identity): We have two options: 1) relax server validation to accept both base64url and base64 (allow +,/ and optional = padding) and normalize to base64url internally, or 2) ask customer to update client lib. Option 1 is low-risk and should be OK as long as we still check length and entropy. I'll prototype a permissive validator that strips padding and replaces +/ with -_.

nina (devex): quick patch idea: replace `state = strings.TrimRight(state, "=")` then `state = strings.ReplaceAll(state, "+", "-")` and same for `/`->`_` before our existing validation. Add test vectors.

jeff (eng-identity): I'll open a PR now, include tests for padded/base64 and base64url. Plan: deploy to staging in the next 2 hours, smoke test with Acme's sample, then roll to prod behind a feature flag.

deploy-bot: :rocket: deploy started for identity-service branch `accept-padded-state` -> staging

luke (eng-sre): After staging smoke we should watch callback error rate metric and set alert if 5xx/400s spike. I'll stand by for prod cutover.

maya (support): Awesome — told Acme we'll test with them on staging first, then do a quick prod rollout. I'll update ticket with timeline. Thanks everyone :pray:

jeff (eng-identity): PR: https://git.redwood/identity/pulls/421 — notes about backward compatibility. I'll tag @luke for rollout plan.

nina (devex): Leaving a note to add a short doc in devex/oauth-quirks about mobile WebViews sending non-urlsafe base64 — could save time next time.

maya (support): Follow-up: Acme validated staging flow, login now succeeds in their WebView. They asked whether this was a security risk — I told them we normalize, keep entropy checks, and won't accept empty/short states.

jeff (eng-identity): Correct. We'll add unit tests for minimum entropy (at least 16 bytes raw), so relaxing the charset doesn't weaken checks. Will merge and schedule prod deploy after 30m canary.

luke (eng-sre): Canary done, no regressions after 45m. Rolling to all regions.

maya (support): Customer confirmed prod fix works, closing ticket. :white_check_mark:
